name: Make a bag from a pattern
blurb: The step from mending to making. A lined tote teaches pattern reading, seam allowances, topstitching and the small order-of-operations tricks that make things look shop-bought.
gear: Outer and lining fabric, plus interfacing
Pins, a rotary cutter or shears, an iron
steps: Read the whole pattern before cutting anything, and note the seam allowance it assumes.
Cut accurately — with fabric, most wonky results start at the cutting stage.
Apply interfacing to give the bag structure, which is what separates a crisp bag from a floppy one.
Sew the outer and lining separately, pressing every seam open as you go. Pressing is not optional.
Learn to box the corners so the bag has a base, and to attach handles securely with a reinforcing square.
Join lining to outer, leaving a turning gap, then close it with a neat topstitch.
tips: Press after every seam. It is the single biggest difference between homemade and handmade.
Handles take all the strain. Reinforce them more than the pattern suggests.
proof: A lined bag with straight topstitching, square corners and handles that survive a heavy load.
